processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Specimen (cylindrical Φ8 mm × 12 mm) heated to 1200 °C at 10 °C/s.
Homogenized by holding at 1200 °C for 120 s.
Cooled to the set deformation temperature T (1150 °C) at a rate of 5 °C/s.
Held for 15 s at the set T before compression so the temperature difference between the inside and outside of the sample was the same.

processing_steps.method: isothermal constant-strain-rate hot compression (Gleeble-3500 thermo-mechanical simulator)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Isothermal constant-strain-rate compression at 1150 °C and strain rate 0.01 s^-1 to 60% height reduction (true strain 0.92). Mica foils with high-temperature lubricants affixed to the two end faces to reduce friction and deformation non-uniformity.
After compression the sample was sprayed with water to cool the steel down.

structures.overall_structure: Initial (pre-deformation) microstructure of the as-forged FeeMneAleC steel billet: large polygonal grains delimited by bright, continuous, slightly etched boundaries, with dark grey grain interiors containing abundant fine, closely spaced parallel light-grey striations (dendritic/interdendritic segregation banding); striation direction changes from grain to grain.

phases_present.morphology: large polygonal grains with bright etched boundaries
phases_present.texture: intragranular parallel striations (segregation banding); striation direction changes from grain to grain

average_grain_size.value: large; individual grains span roughly one to a few times the 100 µm scale bar (not reported numerically)

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: large polygonal grains, heterogeneous contrast (some grains featureless, others densely striped)

structures.overall_structure: After 60% (true strain 0.92) hot compression at 1150 °C and 0.01 s^-1: the material underwent dynamic recrystallization and the recrystallized grains grew rapidly, giving a coarse-grain structure.

microstructure_list.region: large deformation zone (core of the compressed sample, where grain size was measured)

average_grain_size.value: >70 μm (structure is coarse grain; Fig. 10 0.01 s^-1 curve at 1150 °C reaches just below the 80 µm gridline)

grain_structure.grain_size_distribution: coarse recrystallized grain structure; recrystallized grains grown rapidly under this condition

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Isothermal constant-strain-rate hot compression (Gleeble-3500) to 60% height reduction (true strain 0.92); mica foils with high-temperature lubricant at the sample end faces; post-deformation water-spray cooling.

ultimate_tensile_strength.note: Peak (rheological/flow) stress of the hot-compression stress-strain curve at 1150 °C, 0.01 s^-1

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Flow (rheological) stress curve at 1150 °C, 0.01 s^-1 (Fig. 3a, dark-blue curve): rises to a peak then softens to a plateau; curve stays near 40 MPa overall with a peak of 53.8 MPa.

characterization_methods.technique: Isothermal constant-strain-rate hot compression testing / thermomechanical simulation
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: T = 900–1150 °C, ε̇ = 0.01–10 s^-1 (this sample: 1150 °C, 0.01 s^-1); maximum compression 60% (true strain 0.92); cylindrical Φ8 mm × 12 mm specimen.
characterization_methods.purpose: Acquire rheological stress curves and study hot deformation / DRX behavior.
characterization_methods.key_findings: At 1150 °C, 0.01 s^-1 the peak flow stress is 53.8 MPa.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Compressed sample split in half along the axial axis; ground, polished and etched; etching solution 30% nitric acid alcohol solution (volume fraction).
characterization_methods.purpose: Observe microstructure of different deformation zones and measure DRX grain size.
characterization_methods.key_findings: At 1150 °C, 0.01 s^-1 the structure is coarse grain with grain size exceeding 70 μm.

computational_details.simulation_method: Arrhenius-type hyperbolic-sine constitutive analysis using the dimensionless Zener-Hollomon parameter

analytical_models.equation_role: Relates peak stress, temperature and strain rate to determine the DRX activation energy

parameters.name: k1 (average slope of ln ε̇ vs ln[sinh(ασp)])

analytical_models.model_note: Q_p = 1000·R·k1·k2 = 669.844 kJ mol^-1; this is an average value over the experimental range because the fitted lines are not parallel.

analytical_models.equation_role: Temperature-compensated strain-rate parameter Z = ε̇ exp(Q_p/RT) that normalizes the characteristic stress/strain values
analytical_models.model_note: lnZ decreases with increasing temperature and increases with strain rate; 52.01 is the lowest tabulated lnZ (Table 1).

computational_details.simulation_method: DRX characteristic-value models and DRX average grain-size prediction model; Levenberg-Marquardt regression for finite-element (DEFORM-3D) simulation
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Billet set as a rigid-plastic body and die indenter as a rigid body; semi-symmetric specimen used as the deformation model; friction of the billet/die contact interface set to shear type with value 0.3; convection coefficient between billet and air set as 0.02 N/(s·mm·°C).
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Predicted vs experimental DRX grain size: correlation coefficient R = 0.996 and MRE = 4.53%; absolute error mostly within 3 μm (one point near ~4.2 μm).

analytical_models.model_name: DRX characteristic-value models (Eq. 10): ε_c, σ_c, ε_p, σ_p, ε_s, σ_s vs lnZ
analytical_models.equation_role: Mathematical models of critical, peak and steady-state strain/stress as functions of the Zener-Hollomon parameter (multiple linear regression)
Prediction of DRX average grain size for numerical simulation of hot forming
analytical_models.model_note: Correlation coefficient R = 0.996 and MRE = 4.53% for all samples.

unmapped_findings: This sample (1150 °C, 0.01 s^-1) has the lowest lnZ = 52.01 of all studied conditions (Table 1; lnZ decreases with increasing T and decreasing ε̇).

At low strain rate (0.01 s^-1) the peak stress decreases from 305.4 MPa at 900 °C to 53.8 MPa at 1150 °C, a reduction of 82%; the steel is a negative temperature-sensitive and positive strain-rate-sensitive material, and the peak stress can be reduced by decreasing ε̇ or increasing T.

The specimen geometry was a cylindrical Φ8 mm × 12 mm sample; the maximum compression was 60% corresponding to a maximum true strain of 0.92; after testing the sample was split in half along the axial axis for microstructure observation.
The reported experimental phenomena (flow-stress dependence and DRX behavior) are stated to have reproducibility for the same steel batch under identical experimental conditions.

Fine and uniform grains are recommended by the study for hot working in 950–1000 °C/0.01–0.1 s^-1 and 1050–1100 °C/1–10 s^-1; the condition of this sample (1150 °C/0.01 s^-1) instead produces coarse grains (grain size exceeding 70 μm) because recrystallized grains grow rapidly at high T and low ε̇.
